\chapter{Wake Model Calibration}
The engineering wake model describes the velocity deficit downstream
of a turbine as
\begin{equation}
\frac{u}{U_0} = 1 - \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - C_T}}{(1 + 2 k x / D)^2},
\end{equation}
where $k$ is the wake decay constant, $C_T$ the thrust coefficient,
$x$ the downstream distance and $D$ the rotor diameter.
For the calibration we used SCADA records from the full year 2025,
filtered to sectors with free inflow from the southwest.

Measured inflow conditions for the forty-eight turbines are listed
below; each entry is the ten-minute mean over the stable periods
selected by the availability filter.

\hline

The fitted decay constant scatters between 0.030 and 0.045 across
the array, with the inner rows showing the largest values.
The next chapter checks what this spread implies for fatigue loads.

\chapter{Load Implications}
The wake-added turbulence raises the fatigue damage equivalent
loads on the downstream machines.
Blade root bending moments were computed with the aeroelastic
model under the calibrated wake field.

\section{Method}
Each turbine was simulated for the six governing sectors,
and the damage equivalent moments were aggregated with a
Woehler exponent of ten for the blade laminates.

\section{Findings}
The centre-row machines carry the highest damage equivalent
loads, about eleven percent above the free-stream reference.
The edge machines see almost no wake-added loading during
southwesterly inflow and remain the production leaders.

\chapter{Meteorological Mast Campaign}
The met mast stands two kilometres west of the array and has
recorded sonic anemometer data at 20~Hz for eleven months.
Cup anemometers at four levels were calibrated in the wind
tunnel before deployment and again after the campaign.

The shear exponent $\alpha_1_2$ derived from the 60~m and 80~m
levels averages 0.19 over stable nights and drops below 0.10
during convective afternoons.
These values feed directly into the inflow model used for the
wake calibration of the previous chapters.

Data recovery reached 96~percent over the campaign;
the gap in March followed a lightning strike on the junction box.
